coordinates.note: REVIEW REQUIRED: no geodetic coordinate for the 4850 Level caverns could be retrieved. This is the surface position of the SURF site from OpenStreetMap, used as a proxy; the DUNE publication and the facility site establish only that the far detector is at the 4850 ft level at Lead, South Dakota. A17 asks for a non-geocoder source for underground_lab coordinates and that requirement is not met.
coordinates.quote: a far detector located at the 4850 ft level of Sanford Underground Research Facility (SURF), in Lead, South Dakota, USA

depth.note: Rock overburden of the 4850-foot level; a 2024 paper by the same author gives 1490 m.

name: SURF 4850 Level — LBNF/DUNE far detector caverns
notes: Coordinates unresolved to detector precision; see the coordinates note.

summary.plain: Caverns nearly a mile underground at the Sanford laboratory, excavated to hold the huge liquid-argon detectors of the DUNE experiment.
summary.technical: LBNF far-site campus on the 4850-foot level of SURF: two detector caverns and a central utility cavern, about 1500 m of rock (4300 m.w.e.) overburden, hosting the DUNE far detector modules.
